name: Ho Chi Minh City
provinceNote: A centrally run city. Since 1 July 2025 it includes the former Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The walkable center is still the old core.
summary: The former Saigon, a walking city of street food and markets. Eat cơm tấm and hủ tiếu, walk Nguyễn Huệ from the cathedral to the palace, shop Bến Thành, and see the War Remnants Museum.
timeNeeded: A walking day in the old core, longer with Chợ Lớn
fee: No single city ticket. Palace and museum adult prices are listed at more than one figure.
getThere: Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre.
seoTitle: Ho Chi Minh City travel guide — street food, Nguyen Hue, Ben Thanh, War Remnants
seoDescription: Eat cơm tấm and hủ tiếu, walk Nguyễn Huệ past the cathedral to the Reunification Palace, shop Bến Thành, and see the War Remnants Museum. Tân Sơn Nhất is 7 km from the centre.
intro: You come to walk Nguyễn Huệ and eat along the way: cơm tấm and hủ tiếu in the lanes, the cathedral at the head of Đồng Khởi, the Reunification Palace a few streets over, then Bến Thành and the War Remnants Museum. Many residents still say Sài Gòn. Nguyễn Huệ runs from City Hall, which is not open to the public, down toward Bạch Đằng, and it is liveliest at sundown. The post office sits opposite the cathedral.

Stay if the walking center is the trip. Go on to Củ Chi or the Mekong if the day outside the city is the trip. Chợ Lớn is a half-day inside this city, at Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu. From 1 August 2025 the palace-only ticket is 40,000 đồng for an adult and the palace-plus-exhibition ticket is 80,000 đồng. The palace homepage lists an adult at 80,000 đồng, and an older attractions line lists 15,000 đồng. The museum’s terms from 1 October 2026 list an adult at 60,000 đồng, against that same older 15,000 đồng line.
gettingAround: Tân Sơn Nhất is the airport, 7 km from the centre, with taxis, ride-hailing, and city buses.

Metro Line 1 runs from Bến Thành toward the east, about 19.7 km with 14 stations. The project page and the December 2024 opening put the eastern end at Bến xe Suối Tiên, with a 29-minute ride and an initial clock of 05:00–22:00. Visit HCMC names Bến xe Miền Đông as the eastern end. The 2024 fares were 6,000–20,000 đồng a ride, with day and month passes in that article. The Saigon Waterbus, public bicycles, and more than 150 bus routes also run. Cross with a slow, steady pace. Rush hours are 7:00–9:00 and 16:30–18:30.

stayAreas.name: Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ
stayAreas.summary: A room within a walk of Đồng Khởi and Nguyễn Huệ puts the cathedral square and the walking street on foot. Bùi Viện is the other night, where it crosses Phạm Ngũ Lão, Đề Thám, and Đỗ Quang Đẩu.

eat: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, bánh mì, bánh xèo, gỏi cuốn, and cà phê sữa đá are the plates. This city mixes regions. Phở is at its best in Hanoi, and hủ tiếu is the bowl that belongs here.
The food guide is the streets and the three fine-dining rooms.
interestsBody: Street food first, then the walk down Nguyễn Huệ, Bến Thành, and the War Remnants Museum. Chợ Lớn is the half-day inside the city.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Cơm tấm is the plate Vietnam Tourism calls essential here. Hủ tiếu is the bowl Vietnam Tourism says is best in this city.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Cơm tấm, hủ tiếu, the snail streets, and the three fine-dining rooms the national page names.

interestGroups.title: Shopping
interestGroups.summary: Bến Thành faces Quách Thị Trang, with the clock tower over the metro square. Vincom Center is the mall named with the walking streets.

cards.title: Ben Thanh Market
cards.summary: The clock tower and the name, on the square where the metro station sits. The food stalls are at the end of the hall.

cards.title: Vincom Center Dong Khoi
cards.summary: Visit HCMC names it with Saigon Centre–Takashimaya. The signs on the corner read Lê Thánh Tôn and Đồng Khởi.

interestGroups.title: Dong Khoi and the cathedral square
interestGroups.summary: The twin-spired cathedral at the head of Đồng Khởi, the post office opposite, the opera along the street, and Nguyễn Huệ at sundown.

cards.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral
cards.summary: Both towers and the rose window. The post office is the building opposite.

cards.title: Central Post Office
cards.summary: The hall opposite the cathedral. Two pages do not name the same architect.

cards.title: Opera House
cards.summary: The facade on Đồng Khởi. A night show is a separate ticket.

cards.title: Nguyen Hue
cards.summary: The walking street from City Hall to Bạch Đằng. Vietnam Tourism says it is liveliest at sundown.

interestGroups.title: The war record
interestGroups.summary: The palace on Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa and the museum on Võ Văn Tần. Their prices do not match the older 15,000 đồng line.

blocks.heading: The palace and the museum
paragraphs: From 1 August 2025 the palace-only ticket is 40,000 đồng for an adult and the palace-plus-exhibition ticket is 80,000 đồng. The homepage lists an adult at 80,000 đồng. Vietnam Tourism’s attractions page lists 15,000 đồng.
From 1 October 2026 the museum’s own terms list 60,000 đồng for an adult. The attractions page lists 15,000 đồng. Pupils and students on the museum page use a free online ticket.

cards.title: Reunification Palace
cards.summary: The halls on the old Norodom site, and the basement command center. The ticket page and the homepage do not list the same adult price.

cards.title: War Remnants Museum
cards.summary: Three floors of artifacts and photographs, and aircraft in the courtyard. The operator’s adult price from 1 October 2026 is 60,000 đồng.

interestGroups.title: Cho Lon
interestGroups.summary: The Chinese neighborhood Vietnam Tourism tells you to walk. Bình Tây and Thiên Hậu are the halls. Chợ Lớn stays an area of this city.

cards.title: Binh Tay Market
cards.summary: The wholesale hall in Chợ Lớn. The gate carries the clock and the name. Bến Thành’s hours do not apply.

cards.title: Thien Hau Temple
cards.summary: The hall of Thiên Hậu in Chợ Lớn. Visit HCMC dates the building to 1760.

interestGroups.title: Sidewalk coffee
interestGroups.summary: Cà phê sữa đá in the park outside the palace, and the sidewalk glass at Turtle Lake.

cards.title: Cà phê sữa đá
cards.summary: The Saturday morning cup outside the palace, and cloth-filter coffee.

faqs.q: Is Ho Chi Minh City the same as Saigon?
faqs.a: Visit HCMC says the city is still widely called Sài Gòn. Ho Chi Minh City is the official name. Since 1 July 2025, Resolution 202/2025/QH15 joins the former city with Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and Bình Dương. The center you walk is the old core.

Resolution 202/2025/QH15 gives 6,772.59 km² and 14,002,598 people. An April 2025 proposal gave 6,772.65 km² and 13,706,632 people. A feast-streets page says nearly 9 million. No single coordinate was published, so there is no map pin.

Cơm tấm, which Vietnam Tourism calls the go-to breakfast and also an any-meal plate. Bánh mì starts a morning on the city itinerary. Cà phê sữa đá is the Saturday cup in the park outside the palace. Chợ Tân Định is the Sunday morning market on Hai Bà Trưng, in District 3 on that itinerary.

season.label: Drier from December to April
season.note: Vietnam Tourism says December to April is drier, sunny, and less humid, and May to November brings short afternoon showers. It is hot all year.
